Sort the rods by their ends. Every joint needs one **male** (external) thread going into one **female** (internal) thread. A male thread screws in completely, so it adds no length.

Unfold in reverse order. Each unfold reflects every hole across that crease, like a mirror. So two holes facing each other across a crease always **lean opposite ways**.

- The folds go right half over left, then top down, then right over left again. That leaves the **bottom-left eighth** of the sheet. The cut there sits low, near the left edge, and leans like **/**.
- Unfold the last vertical fold: a **\\** appears next to it, mirrored across the crease.
- Unfold the horizontal fold: the top row is the bottom row flipped, so each hole changes lean.
- Unfold the first vertical fold: the right half mirrors the left.

Result: bottom row **/ \\ / \\**, top row **\\ / \\ /**. That is **A**.
- **B**: top row is / / \\ \\. Holes facing each other across the quarter creases lean the same way, which a mirror can't produce.
- **C**: same problem (\\ \\ / /).
- **D**: top and bottom rows are swapped, so the bottom-left hole leans \\, not the / that was cut.
